section_summary.extract_value: This section details supplemental analyses conducted on team communication records from a task using TIDE^2 software. It describes the measurement of interpersonal, transition, and action processes across three phases of team activity. The analyses investigated how team composition (learning and performance orientation) and goal difficulty predicted these processes, and how these processes, in turn, predicted team adaptation. Key findings include that interpersonal and transition processes during disruption positively affected adaptation, while action processes during disruption had a negative effect, but promoted adaptation after stabilization. The section also highlights interactions between goal orientation and goal difficulty in predicting team processes.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details supplemental analyses conducted on team communication records from a single study. Doctoral students rated team communications across three phases (predisruption, disruption, postdisruption) for interpersonal, transition, and action processes. HGLM models revealed that processes during disruption predicted adaptation, with interpersonal and transition processes having a positive effect and action processes a negative effect. Performance orientation was found to interact with goal difficulty in predicting these processes, with high-performance orientation teams with difficult goals showing poorer interpersonal processes and decreased communication regarding performance progress after disruption.

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes supplemental analyses conducted on text message communications among team members using TIDE^2 software. Doctoral-level students rated team communications on interpersonal, transition, and action processes during three phases: post-training, during disruption, and post-disruption. HGLM models were used to predict adaptation from these processes, with results appearing in Table 4. OLS regression was used to predict these processes from team composition variables and goal difficulty, with statistically significant models presented in Table 5 and interactions plotted in Figures 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8. The analyses revealed how goal difficulty and goal orientation jointly determine adaptive or maladaptive team behavior patterns.
